paper.title: The EAGLE project: Simulating the evolution and assembly of galaxies and their environments
paper.authors: Joop Schaye, Robert A. Crain, Richard G. Bower et al.

thesis: EAGLE constitutes a valuable new resource for studies of galaxy formation.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What does the reported model reveal when the target system is simulated?

nodes.title: Choose model and boundary conditions
nodes.body: The observed galaxy mass function is reproduced to $\lesssim 0.2$ dex over the full mass range, $10^8 < M_*/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{11}$, a level of agreement close to that attained by semi-analytic models, and unprecedented for hydrodynamical simulations.

nodes.title: Run the numerical experiment
nodes.body: We introduce the Virgo Consortium's EAGLE project, a suite of hydrodynamical simulations that follow the formation of galaxies and black holes in representative volumes.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: We compare our results to a representative set of low-redshift observables not considered in the calibration, and find good agreement with the observed galaxy specific star formation rates, passive fractions, Tully-Fisher relation, total stellar luminosities of galaxy clusters, and column density distributions of intergalactic CIV and OVI.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: EAGLE constitutes a valuable new resource for studies of galaxy formation.
